planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix; Propeller Plant is extremely drought-tolerant and rots quickly in wet or dense soil.

directions: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix. Propeller Plant produces thick, grey-green, curved, sickle-shaped leaves arranged in tightly stacked, opposite pairs that spiral up a stout upright stem, giving each pair the look of a small propeller blade and the whole plant a distinctive architectural silhouette unlike the rounded rosettes of most other succulents. Large, dense, flattened clusters of small, brilliant orange-red flowers appear at the stem tips in summer, a striking bloom against the muted grey foliage that draws butterflies. Water only when the soil has dried out completely, since it is highly susceptible to root and stem rot in constantly moist conditions, and give it the brightest light available for the strongest leaf color and most compact growth.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded hanging container in bright indirect light to partial sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix; Calico Kitten tolerates lower light than most other Crassula species.

directions: Grow in bright indirect light to partial sun in fast-draining, gritty succulent mix, in a hanging basket or elevated pot where the trailing stems can cascade. Calico Kitten forms trailing stems of small, heart-shaped, semi-translucent leaves marbled in shades of cream, pink, and green, with the pink and cream tones intensifying in brighter light and cooler weather, giving it a soft, variegated, calico-cat-like coloring quite different from the solid green or grey succulents most people picture. Its delicate, cascading habit and smaller leaf size make it a favorite for mixed succulent hanging baskets and dish gardens where a trailing accent is wanted. Water only when the soil has dried out completely, since overwatering is the most common cause of rot in the soft, fleshy stems and leaves.

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or xeriscape container in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix; Campfire Plant develops its brightest red color under stress from bright light and lean, dry conditions.

directions: Grow in bright light to full sun in fast-draining, gritty cactus-and-succulent mix, watering thoroughly then allowing the mix to dry completely before watering again. Campfire Plant forms low, spreading rosettes of tightly stacked, triangular leaves that start green but flush an intense, fiery orange-red at the tips and outer edges under strong sun and lean, dry conditions, giving the whole clump a glowing, flame-like coloring that gives the plant its common name. It spreads readily by short offsets to form a dense mat over time, useful as a groundcover in a xeriscape rock garden or as a colorful accent trailing over a container edge. Reduce watering and maximize light exposure for the most vivid red coloring, since shade and excess moisture cause the plant to green out and stretch.
